title: Understanding Cross-Validation
text: Cross-validation is a technique used to assess the performance of a model by partitioning the data into subsets, training the model on some subsets, and validating it on others.

title: Bias in Cross-Validation
text: Increasing the number of folds (k) in k-fold cross-validation generally reduces the bias of the model because it allows the model to be trained and validated on more diverse subsets of the data.

title: Computational Intensity of Cross-Validation
text: Cross-validation is typically more computationally intensive than regular validation because it involves training and validating the model multiple times, once for each fold.

title: Using Entire Dataset in Cross-Validation
text: One advantage of cross-validation is that it allows the model to be tested on the entire dataset, as each data point is used for both training and validation across different folds.

title: Cross-Validation in Production
text: Cross-validation is not typically used in production environments because it is primarily a model evaluation technique used during the development phase to estimate model performance.
